newsitem.title: USA: AWAY ON BUSINESS - More dial-up info.
newsitem.headline: AWAY ON BUSINESS - More dial-up info.

text.p: The amount of online information aimed at business travelers -- from weather reports to airline schedules -- seems to grow daily.
One of the newest is an Internet site established by Business Travel News -- a high-end publication circulated primarily to travel managers and corporate executives.
The publication is trying to broaden its name recognition and reach other travel consumers through its address at http:/www.btonline.com.
"We are trying to reach beyond our core audience, which is familiar with the publication, and allow typical business travelers to learn something," a spokeswoman said.
A recent check of the site found a wide variety of news items, some of them previously published but still of interest to readers who don't keep up and need to find a broad sample under one tent.

The site reports, for example, that Air France's against-the-grain move on smoking seems to be drawing enough customer support that it will be expanded. The carrier last year began putting in "smoker's bars" -- curtained-off, ventilated sections on larger airlines -- for use by smokers.

The lounges are available on certain, long-haul flights leaving Newark, New York, Houston, Los Angeles and San Francisco, it reports, and will be expanded to flights from Chicago and Miami later this year.
Smoking has been banned voluntarily and by regulation on a growing number of airlines, including some operating international routes.
The site also offers fingertip information on major international destinations from Baltimore to Tehran, Singapore to Cleveland, complete with government, cultural and weather information.
The section on Vientiane, Laos, for example, even includes the CIA Factbook on that country.
There are also sections on bargains and other promotions being offered by hotels and airlines.
On another front, frequent travelers tired of crowded airline flights will apparently find little relief this winter. Surveys indicated continued heavy travel conditions.

Some routes, however, will be more crowded than others. Carlson Wagonlit Travel reports that a survey of its agents found that the most popular travel destination from the United States to Canada this winter is Mexico, followed by the Caribbean, Florida, various cruise ship ports and Hawaii.
California and Colorado were sixth and seventh. The agents polled reported that from 20 to 50 percent of their clients planned on taking winter vacations.

Business travelers: Question, complaint or pet peeve? Send them to Away on Business, c/o Reuters, Room 1170, 311 S. Wacker Dr., Chicago 60606. Or via Internet E-mail Mike.Conlon(at)Reuters.com using the "at" sign on computer keyboards. We cannot promise personal replies but will try to address letters as space permits.
